$comment: Gemfall beat 1, The Spark. Story: docs/campaigns/gemfall.md §1. Wiring: docs/campaigns/gemfall-authoring.md. Must set on every path to every ending: exactly one motive_* (choice_why_north, which every path passes through) and exactly one of ember_sold / ember_kept (choice_ember, which every path passes through). The six motive votes each land on a short result scene (scene_motive_*) before the docks, so the vote is seen to matter at the table. Mostly people, prices and promises, with one gentle fight on the spine: two wisps drawn to the warm Ember Facet tangle the quay lamps (scene_quay_wisps, encounter_quay_wisps), which every road walks between the tavern and Madame Fenn; a lost fight is a cocoa rescue that rejoins at choice_ember, never a setback. Expansion: the prologue ends on a vote (what the party was doing on the docks that night), and each pick pays off later in the chapter: the lamps open Old Wick's path over the Long Bridge, the oranges buy the sailors' rumors, the sardine feeds the gull. Further episodes: the jammed Long Bridge, the Griffin Post (whose friends can vouch for the stone), the gull, Mrs. Tuft's provision barge, Mortar's goodbye (whose word gets you hired by Hesper), and the North Gate on the way out. Second pass: a selkie family arriving on the quay (help them, and they make room for you when the Empty Chair inn is full) and the full inn itself. Interactions on the spine: the pear line (relay), the letters (timing), Mrs. Tuft's jar tray (balance) and the lantern pole (cooperate).
title: The City That Smelled Opportunity

objectives.label: Listened to the scholar everyone laughed at
Heard the rumors of all three roads north
Signed on as real caravan crew

goal.text: Get ready for the long trip north.

steps.label: Find a bed for the night

facet_ember.name: The Ember Facet
facet_ember.text: A red stone, warm as toast, that fell from the sky into an Exchange gutter by your boot.

scene_prologue_realm.narration: This is the Realm of Red Sky. Far north stands Mount Red Sky, source of the Gemfalls. Old maps say it is only sleeping. Get ready for the long trip north: tonight your story begins at the Exchange docks.

choices.label: Go on

scene_prologue_city.narration: The Exchange stands where roads and rivers meet the sea. Travelers trade goods, news and chances to begin again. Nobody is from here. That is rather the point.

choices.label: Go on

scene_prologue_party.narration: You met on the docks this week. Between you: a shared purse of six coins, one supper bundle, and reasons for traveling you have not told yet. Harbor lamps are coming on. What are you doing here tonight?

choices.label: Fishing off the end of the long pier
Helping a ship unload its oranges
Helping the old lamplighter light the lamps
Doing card tricks for the sailors

scene_prologue_party_prologue_begin.narration: One bucket, several fishing lines: two old boots and a silver sardine. You tuck the sardine away. A gull watches it. The sardine, as much as sardines can, watches back.

choices.label: Keep fishing while the stars come out

scene_prologue_party_oranges.narration: You help unload the Sunny Disposition. Its yeti captain has orange peel in his fur. "We owe you one. Sailors pay their debts." He thinks. "Mostly in oranges."

choices.label: Sit on a crate and peel an orange

scene_prologue_party_lamps.narration: Old Wick, a frogfolk lamplighter, names every lamp as he lights it. You carry his ladder. He shows you a quiet ledge along the Long Bridge. "Nobody else looks."

choices.label: Light the last lamp at the end of the harbor

scene_prologue_party_cards.narration: Your kitsune does card tricks on an upturned barrel. A sailor picks a card, and it turns up in his own boot. Then in his hat. Then in his sandwich. The sailors laugh so hard that one of them gives you his lucky stone, a smooth pebble with a hole in it. "You clearly don't need luck," he says, "so it'll be safe with you."

choices.label: Shuffle up for one more trick

scene_red_sky.narration: The northern sky turns cherry red. Gem-light rains over the foothills. For a blink, some falls upward. A gull drops its fish. Both look surprised.

choices.label: Fly up the lighthouse for a better look
Watch from the harbor wall
Run down to the docks and see what people do

scene_lighthouse.narration: From the lighthouse, one thread of gem-light rises toward the mountain. The old merfolk keeper sits up in her bathtub. Officially, she saw nothing. Neither did you.

choices.label: Glide back down and see what the city does

scene_harbour_wall.narration: Ships swing on their anchors until their noses point north. Tower bells ring, then stop. Nobody knows this signal. The lighthouse lamp shuts one eye and pretends it did not.

choices.label: Watch the red fade, and see what the morning brings

scene_night_docks.narration: A boy changes the rope price on his ladder. A merfolk in a wheeled barrel shouts "Rush prices!" A fishmonger looks north and doubles the herring price.

choices.label: Find a crate to sit on and watch it all begin

scene_stampede.narration: Three days later, the Exchange is packed. Everybody says gems. Prices rise while you read them. Before going north, you need a reason, road news, food, a bed and a caravan. First, find somewhere to talk.

choices.label: Read the brass plaques on the harbor
Find somewhere to sit down and talk

scene_plaques.narration: Seventeen harbor plaques name seventeen different founders. One says MY GRANDMA. A centaur guide says everybody belongs here. Today the explanation is free, because you look new.

choices.label: Find somewhere to sit down and talk

scene_long_bridge.narration: The noodle stall is beyond the jammed Long Bridge. A goat stands on a merchant who has not noticed. Nobody can move. The cabbage barge below is doing much better.

choices.label: Squeeze through the crowd
Ride the cabbage barge under the bridge
Take Old Wick's lamplighters' path
Wade the canal beside the bridge
Have a duskrunner lead us through the crowd

check_bridge_squeeze.prompt: Wriggle across a bridge where nobody can move

onSuccess.narration: You go sideways, then under a cart, then over a very patient yeti, and pop out of the far end like a cork from a bottle. The noodle stall is right there.

onFailure.narration: The crowd swallows you up and carries you the whole way across without your feet touching the ground once. It sets you down very politely, facing the wrong way, right beside the noodle stall.

scene_long_bridge_barge.narration: You ride the cabbage barge under hundreds of dangling feet. It costs nothing. You reach the noodle stall smelling strongly of cabbage.

choices.label: Climb off and shake out the cabbage leaves

scene_long_bridge_lamp_path.narration: Old Wick's ledge is clear. You cross above the traffic. Halfway over, he is lighting a lamp at noon, just to be sure. He tips his hat.

choices.label: Hop down by the noodle stall

scene_long_bridge_wade.narration: Your bigfoot steps off the bank into the canal. It comes up to their knees. Everybody else climbs onto their shoulders, and then two strangers climb on too, and then the goat. You wade across like a walking tower, and the whole bridge cheers you all the way to the noodle stall.

choices.label: Set everybody down, goat last

choice_why_north.narration: You find an empty chair at Mortar's noodle stall. "Every table keeps one for whoever comes next," the stone troll says. "Today, that is you." Why is your party going north?

choices.label: For the treasure. Gems, gems, gems!
To find out what really happened
So everyone will know our names
Because somebody has to keep folk safe
For a fresh start somewhere new
To prove we can do it

scene_motive_wealth.narration: Mortar, the noodle stall's stone troll, chalks RUSH PRICES on his board. Your noodles are free. Three pickpockets move one table closer.

choices.label: Go and find out what gems are fetching at the docks

scene_motive_curiosity.narration: Mortar, the noodle stall's stone troll, stops stirring. "The gull dropped its fish before the light arrived. Heard something first." He has clearly thought about this for three days.

choices.label: Go and ask the docks what they heard

scene_motive_prestige.narration: Mortar, the noodle stall's stone troll, writes your names under TODAY'S HEROES. One is misspelled. A faun asks you to sign her dumpling, then eats it for safekeeping.

choices.label: Go where the news is made: the docks

scene_motive_duty.narration: Mortar, the noodle stall's stone troll, sets out an extra bowl. "For whoever needs it." A stranded faun eats, spots her cousins' wagon, and runs after it waving the spoon.

choices.label: Wave her off and head down to the docks

scene_motive_fresh_start.narration: Mortar, the noodle stall's stone troll, marks your empty chair. "Yours now. Everyone here started again." He gives you bread, which at rush prices is practically a house.

choices.label: Take your first steps as new people: down to the docks

scene_motive_proving.narration: Mortar, the noodle stall's stone troll, points at the Big Bowl. "Nobody finishes it." You finish it together. Somebody has to be rolled away afterward. "Hm," says Mortar. Applause, for a troll.

choices.label: Waddle down to the docks, victorious

scene_newcomers.narration: A selkie family steps ashore with everything they own. Rush prices make them go quiet. "Up the hill, the Empty Chair inn has room for newcomers," their grandmother says. The harbor plaques name selkie founders too. Everybody else hurries north.

choices.label: Carry their bags to the Empty Chair inn
Walk them along the brass plaques on the quay
Tell them we're starting fresh too
Risk lifting the whole load without leveling it

check_newcomers_carry.prompt: Carry a whole family's luggage up the busiest street in the realm

onSuccess.narration: Trunks, bundles, a rocking chair and a fishbowl with a very calm fish in it: you carry the lot up the hill without dropping a thing. The selkies take a room at the Empty Chair, and the five children wave from the window until you turn the corner.

onFailure.narration: Halfway up the hill the biggest trunk pops open, and out pour about a hundred knitted socks. All five children help you chase them down the street. It takes ages, and it is the most fun anybody has had all week. The selkies take a room at the Empty Chair, socks and all.

scene_newcomers_plaque.narration: The grandmother reads the selkie founder's plaque twice. "Then we are home." She gives you her river charm for the road. Her grandchildren straighten the plaque.

choices.label: Wave goodbye and head for the docks

scene_newcomers_fresh.narration: You swap fresh-start advice: eat at Mortar's, ignore the prices, keep an empty chair. The selkies take a room at the inn and promise to save space for you.

choices.label: Head down to the docks

scene_docks.narration: The docks trade news. A boggart in a coat of other coats sells "slightly used rumors." The yeti fishmonger shouts road news between herring prices.

choices.label: Listen in on the dock folk's rumors
Buy a rumor from the boggart
Read the crowd and hear what nobody says out loud
Find the orange ship's sailors. They owe us one

scene_docks_sailors.narration: The crew of the Sunny Disposition are mending sails on the quay, and they cheer when they see you. Sailors pay their debts, and they pay this one in rumors: one from every port they stopped at on the way in. The yeti captain throws in an orange each for the road, because he cannot help himself.

choices.label: Tally up everything you heard

check_rumours.prompt: Catch three good rumors out of a whole dock shouting at once

onSuccess.narration: You stand very still in the middle of all that shouting and pick out the good bits: one from a sailor, one from a drover, one from a frogfolk with reeds in her hat. Three rumors, three roads, caught like fish in a net.

onFailure.narration: The dock shouts too fast. You catch half a rumor about a pie and a whole one about somebody's aunt. In the end the yeti fishmonger takes pity on you and says the roads again, slowly, between herrings.

scene_boggart.narration: The boggart's rumors come in little jars with the lids screwed on tight. You pay with a button. You open the jar, and the rumor inside is: "The mountain is grumpy." You already knew that. Then the boggart says it again, slower, looking sideways, off to the west where the marshes are, and you realize it meant something else entirely.

choices.label: Take the jar to the dock folk and ask which road it meant

scene_three_rumours.narration: Three roads: east to Stone Crossing, a story toll and a crowded river; north through the Plains with the packed rush wagons; west through the Whispering Marsh, if the frogfolk like you. The fishmonger points up. "Courier griffins carry so many claim letters they can barely steer."

choices.label: Head back through the market, keeping one eye on the sky

scene_griffin_post.narration: On the way back you pass the Griffin Post, a tall tower full of round windows. Courier griffins line up on the roof while clerks stuff claim letters into their sacks, and then a few more, and then a few more after that. The postmaster, a griffin called Quill with glasses on a chain, is losing count. "Hands!" she squawks. "Anybody with hands!"

choices.label: Help sort the letters
Share our supper with the tired couriers
Talk shop with the couriers
Risk sorting the sacks without checking the route cards

check_post_sort.prompt: Sort nine hundred claim letters before the griffins take off

onSuccess.narration: You sort them by mountain, then by valley, then by how loud the handwriting is. Postmaster Quill is so pleased she gives you a brave whistle, the kind couriers blow to clear the sky.

onFailure.narration: You sort the letters beautifully, into all the wrong sacks. A letter for a duke is now going to a duck. Quill sighs, says it will all come out in the wash, and stuffs everything into one enormous sack anyway.

scene_griffin_post_feed.narration: The couriers have been flying since the red night and have not stopped once for supper. You share yours. One young griffin eats a whole loaf in a single gulp, then a second loaf to check the first one was real. He bows to you with his wings out, which in griffin means: I will remember your faces.

choices.label: Wave them off into the sky

scene_griffin_post_shop.narration: Your griffin and the couriers talk wing to wing about headwinds, sack straps and the worst roofs to land on. Then they lower their voices. Since the red night, no courier will fly within a day of the mountain. "The air up there hums," says one, "like a kettle that's thinking about it." They make you an honorary courier, which mostly means free gossip.

choices.label: Swap one last bit of gossip

scene_gutter_glint.narration: A courier's huge sack splits overhead. Letters flutter over the market. A warm red stone lands by your boot with a plink. It is plum-sized, glittering, and humming.

choices.label: Pick it up and pocket it
Shout "Whose is this?"
Call up to the courier who knows us
Pocket the stone, then catch mail in the checked bags

scene_gutter_glint_griffin.narration: The courier hears you, wobbles around, and lands on a chimney pot with his split sack in his beak. He peers at the red stone. "Not mine," he says. "That didn't come out of my sack. That came out of the sky, after it." He fluffs his feathers. "Finders keepers. Tell nobody I said so."

choices.label: Pocket it, and wave him off

scene_nobody_claims.narration: Eleven people say it is theirs. None of them can say what color it is. The griffin is already a dot over the sea, and the dot is not coming back. It seems the stone is yours, for now.

choices.label: Pocket it and head for the Empty Chair

scene_gull_dive.narration: A gull blocks your way and eyes the warm stone in your pocket. It looks like the gull from the red night. It crouches. You have time to choose before it dives.

choices.label: Grab the gull before it grabs the stone
Offer it your supper instead
Throw it the sardine from the red night
Chase it off on the wing

check_gull_grab.prompt: Catch a seagull in mid-dive, gently

onSuccess.narration: You catch the gull in mid-dive, very gently, like a loaf of bread. It looks embarrassed. You set it down on a post, and it pretends that was where it was going all along.

onFailure.narration: The gull is quicker. It snatches the stone, flaps three circles over the market, finds it is much heavier than a fish, and drops it down the chimney of the nearest tavern. You run in after it and fish it out of the ashes, still warm, and only a little sooty.

scene_gull_dive_bread.narration: You hold out your supper. The gull considers the supper. It considers the stone. It takes the supper, cloth and all. Fair is fair. It flaps away full and happy, and leaves the stone alone. Your tummies rumble all the way to the Empty Chair.

choices.label: Go and find some supper

scene_gull_dive_sardine.narration: The sardine has had a long three days. The gull swallows it, then follows you to the Empty Chair like a small, very loud guard.

choices.label: Leave your new friend on guard

scene_gull_dive_outfly.narration: Wings snap open and up you go. The gull has never been chased by anything bigger than a cat. It flies one loop, sees who is behind it, and decides it had other plans today. A crowd on the quay claps. Two pickpockets who were also watching your pocket decide they had other plans too.

choices.label: Land with a bow by the Empty Chair's door

scene_tavern.narration: At the Empty Chair, a selkie scholar stands on a table. "The gem-light fell upward!" The room laughs. Two polite trolls carry her out, table and all. She keeps talking.

choices.label: Follow her outside
Tell her we saw it too!
Ask what it means. That is why we came, after all
Leave her be. There are gem-buyers to see

scene_scholar_believed.narration: The scholar stops wringing out her notes and stares at you. Then she hugs you, which is very wet, because she is a selkie and it is raining. "Professor Marrow Tidewell," she says, "and you are the first people who have believed me all week." She unpins the owl-feather clasp from her own coat and gives it to you, for clear thinking.

choices.label: Hear the whole theory

scene_scholar_theory.narration: Outside, the scholar draws on a napkin. Professor Tidewell, says the name on her soggy notes. The drawing is a shape with eight sides, like a gem cut by somebody very careful. "The oldest stories tell of a seal, like a lid on a jar, made of facets, eight of them. I think the mountain just threw seven of them across the realm, and everybody is selling them. The eighth is still in the mountain." Then she looks at your pocket, which is glowing slightly. "Oh," she says. "You've got one."

choices.label: Thank her, and think about it

choice_ember.narration: Gem-buyer Madame Coralie Fenn rolls up in her merfolk barrel. "Rush prices, darlings!" She names a huge price for the red stone. A pigeon faints. Sell the stone for coins, or keep its hum with you?

choices.label: Sell it to Madame Fenn
Haggle her up even higher, then sell
Keep it

choice_ember_sell_high.narration: You name a bigger number. Madame Fenn names a smaller one. You name a bigger one again, and a second pigeon faints. In the end she pays twice what she offered, laughs so hard her barrel rolls into a bollard, and throws in a brave whistle "for cheek, darlings." Then she writes your names in her little green book, twice.

choices.label: Take the clanking purse

scene_sold.narration: Fenn pays into a clanking purse and adds a lucky bead. "I never forget a good seller." The humming goes away in her barrel.

choices.label: Go and spend some of it

scene_kept.narration: You close your hand around the warm stone. Fenn sighs so hard her barrel rocks. The hum stays with you. You still need supplies.

choices.label: Go and get ready for the road

scene_provisions.narration: At the Outfitters' Steps, Mrs. Tuft, a sheeple grocer, gives each northbound party one supply. Her price tags stick in her wool. "Food to share, a healing potion, or light for dark roads," she says. "Pick one." Her jars even come in jars.

choices.label: A tin of honeycakes, for sharing
A sunbloom potion, for bumps and scrapes
A jar of mosslight, for dark roads
Show Mrs. Tuft the warm red stone

scene_provisions_honey.narration: Mrs. Tuft packs six honeycakes into a tin, then a seventh "for the tin". You promise to save them for the road. By the top of the Outfitters' Steps there are five. Nobody knows what happened to the other two, and everybody has crumbs on their chin.

choices.label: Climb the steps to the cobbler

scene_provisions_sunbloom.narration: The sunbloom potion glows in its bottle like a little sunrise. "For bumps, scrapes and grumps," says Mrs. Tuft. "Mostly grumps." She wraps it in a sock so it will not clink against anything, and then throws in the sock for free.

choices.label: Climb the steps to the cobbler

scene_provisions_mosslight.narration: The mosslight glows soft and green, like a tiny forest that fits in your hand. "Picked far to the west by my cousins," says Mrs. Tuft. "It likes to be talked to. Not sung to. It's very particular." The jar seems to brighten a little when you say thank you.

choices.label: Climb the steps to the cobbler

scene_provisions_stone.narration: Mrs. Tuft takes one look at the red stone, and every jar on her barge starts to rattle on its shelf, very gently, the way spoons do when a cart goes by. She hands it back rather quickly. "Lovely," she says, not meaning it. She hands you a honeycake in a hurry, and you get the feeling it is so you will leave a bit sooner.

choices.label: Pocket the stone and climb the steps

scene_market.narration: Cobbler Tobble Reedpipe sings the price of quickfoot laces, "Quick feet, sweet price!" Each verse goes higher. By the top of the Outfitters' Steps, he squeaks. You can trade, buy if you have the coins, or save them.

choices.label: Sing the price down with Tobble
Buy the best laces outright. We're rich now!
Tell Tobble we're after a fresh start
Point out the fake laces on the next stall
Keep your coins and go and find a bed

scene_market_keep_coins.narration: You keep your old laces and your coins. Tobble sings you down the steps, one key lower each step. At the bottom, he is humming.

choices.label: Find a bed for the night

scene_market_spot_fakes.narration: Your kitsune sniffs once and points. "Those are bootlaces painted yellow." The stall-keeper next door goes very red, packs up in about four seconds, and is never seen on the Outfitters' Steps again. Tobble is so grateful he presses real quickfoot laces on you and sings your names up the whole scale.

choices.label: Lace up

scene_market_fresh_start.narration: Tobble stops singing. "A fresh start," he says, and for once he just speaks. He has one too, he says. He used to make boots for a duke, and then he decided he liked laces better. He sells you the laces at last year's price and sings a small verse about beginnings that nearly rhymes.

choices.label: Lace up

scene_market_buy_outright.narration: You point at the best laces on the rack and pay without asking the price. Tobble is so startled he sings the price anyway, out of habit, a whole key too high. Three prospectors turn around to see who is rich. You try to look like you have always been rich.

choices.label: Lace up

check_haggle.prompt: Sing the price back to Tobble, one key lower, without losing the tune

onSuccess.narration: You sing back, one key lower. Tobble is so delighted he sells you the laces at last week's price.

onFailure.narration: You sing back, but your note lands somewhere Tobble's song has never been. He loses his place and starts again from the top, twice. Somewhere in the muddle, money changes hands and something is wrapped in paper.

scene_laced.narration: The quickfoot laces go on, and right away your feet would like to be somewhere else, quickly. Tobble sings a little verse about you. It is very flattering and mostly does not rhyme.

choices.label: Find a bed for the night

scene_lace_tangle.narration: Your song and Tobble's get so tangled up that he sells you a honeycake instead of laces. You are not sure how that happened. Neither is Tobble. It is a very good honeycake, though.

choices.label: Find a bed for the night

scene_inn_full.narration: Innkeeper Flint has one cupboard bed and several bidders. His nightcap is much too small. "One warm bed," he rumbles, folding his arms. "Earn it." Share a story, work for the bed, call on friends, or pay if you can.

choices.label: Tell the best story of the red night
Offer to wash the supper bowls for it
Find the selkie family upstairs
Outbid everybody with Madame Fenn's purse
Risk telling the whole story over the noisy room

check_inn_story.prompt: Tell the red night so well a whole inn goes quiet

onSuccess.narration: You tell it all: the cherry-red sky, the gem-light falling, the seagull and its very surprised fish. The whole inn goes quiet. Flint wipes one eye with a dishcloth and hands you the cupboard key without a word.

onFailure.narration: Your story wanders off somewhere around the fish and never quite comes back. The prospectors laugh so kindly that Flint gives the cupboard to someone else and you the hayloft above the mules, which is warm, smells of apples, and is honestly nicer.

scene_inn_full_dishes.narration: There are three hundred supper bowls, and some of them have been used twice. You wash, dry and stack until your fingers go wrinkly as raisins and the kitchen is full of soap bubbles. At midnight Flint inspects one bowl very closely, says "Hm," and hands you the key. The other prospectors are still arguing about prices.

choices.label: Squeeze into the cupboard

scene_inn_full_selkies.narration: The selkie family you helped today hear your voices and come thundering down the stairs. "You'll squash in with us," says the grandmother, and that is the end of the argument. Their room is tiny, and eight selkies is a lot of selkie, but it is warm. The five children want a bedtime story, and they want it about you.

choices.label: Squash in and tell the story

scene_inn_full_outbid.narration: You open Madame Fenn's clanking purse and name a number. The other prospectors go pale and wander off to sleep in the stables. Flint bites one coin to check it is real, then another to check the first one was. The cupboard is yours. It is still a cupboard, but it is the most expensive cupboard in the realm.

choices.label: Admire your very expensive cupboard

rest_empty_chair.narration: Cupboard, hayloft or squashed-up room, it is warm and dry, and somebody shares out supper. Through the wall, three people in three languages argue happily about the price of onions, and all three of them are right. Tomorrow the caravans leave.

choices.label: Up at dawn for the caravan yard

scene_last_noodles.narration: At dawn, Mortar watches you pass with packed bags. He stirs one slow turn. "Going, then." The caravan lanterns are lit. Time for one farewell before the yard.

choices.label: Ask him which caravan to join
Leave a gift on the empty chair
Eat one last bowl, for the road
Let Mortar listen to the warm stone

scene_last_noodles_ask.narration: Mortar stirs one whole slow turn. Then another. "Longstride," he says at last. "Lantern wagon. Listens to the whole answer." He taps the table with one enormous finger. "Tell her Mortar sent you." That is more words than he has said all week, and he looks a bit tired afterwards.

choices.label: Thank him, and head for the lantern wagon

scene_last_noodles_gift.narration: Every table in the Exchange keeps an empty chair for whoever comes next. You leave a button on it, and a note that says GOOD LUCK in all your different handwritings. Underneath, tied to the chair leg, you find a songbird ribbon. Somebody left it there for you, before you ever came. Mortar pretends not to see. He is smiling, very slowly.

choices.label: Tie on the ribbon and go

scene_last_noodles_bowl.narration: Mortar ladles out the biggest breakfast of your lives. When you are done, he unpins the little thistle from his apron and pins it on you. "Strong noodles," he rumbles. "Strong legs." Then, after a long stir: "Come back." Two words, which from a stone troll is practically a speech.

choices.label: Wave goodbye with full tummies

scene_last_noodles_listen.narration: Mortar holds the warm stone to his great stone ear for a long, long time. The whole stall goes quiet. "Sings," he says at last. "Like my grandma's pot, just before it boiled over." He gives it back to you very carefully, the way you hand somebody a baby bird, and fills your water flasks for nothing.

choices.label: Tuck the stone away and go

scene_caravan_yard.narration: Centaur caravan master Hesper Longstride checks the lantern wagon. Her sash is stitched with roads. "Room for another crew." She lowers her clipboard to hear why you want to join.

choices.label: Tell her honestly why we're going
Lift a stuck wagon out of the mud
Offer to guard her lantern wagon
Bet we can load a wagon faster than anyone
Offer to carry the banner at the front
Tell Hesper that Mortar sent us
Have a thornguard stand watch over the lantern wagon
Risk a hurried pitch while Hesper checks the wagons

scene_caravan_yard_banner.narration: The banner is taller than you are and heavier than it looks, and the wind off the harbor wants it very badly. You hold it up anyway. The whole yard turns to look at who is carrying the Longstride banner, and Hesper lets them look. "Front," she says. "Don't drop it."

choices.label: Take your place at the front

scene_caravan_yard_race.narration: A yeti crew bets you cannot load a wagon faster than they can. You load it in the time it takes them to argue about who goes first. Half of it is loaded upside down, but it is loaded. The yetis pay up in dried apples, and Hesper, very slightly, smiles.

choices.label: Collect your winnings

scene_caravan_yard_guard.narration: "The lantern wagon," says Hesper, "has been robbed twice this week and set on fire once." You say you will guard it anyway. She looks at you the way she looks at weather that has decided to be useful, and hands you a long pole with a hook on the end.

choices.label: Take up your post

scene_caravan_yard_lift_wagon.narration: You walk over to the wagon stuck in the mud, take hold of the back axle, and lift. The wagon comes up. So does the mud. So does a small faun who was sitting in the wagon eating breakfast, and who keeps eating it. Hesper watches the whole thing without a word, then nods once.

choices.label: Report for duty

scene_caravan_yard_mortar.narration: Hesper's ears turn right around. "Mortar," she says. "How many words did he say about you?" You count. Four. She is quiet for a moment, the way weather is quiet before it decides something. Then she nods once. From a stone troll, four words is a letter of recommendation.

choices.label: Report for duty

check_signon.prompt: Tell a caravan master the truth and mean it

onSuccess.narration: Hesper listens to the whole answer, all the way to the end. Then she nods once, like a gate closing.

onFailure.narration: You get muddled halfway through and say "um" eleven times. Hesper is kind about it. Hesper is also busy.

scene_hired.narration: Hesper hands you a lantern pole. "Crew." You eat first and sleep last. The wagons roll toward the North Gate, with you on duty.

choices.label: Roll north

scene_turnip_wagon.narration: "Cargo, then," says Hesper, kindly. You ride among turnips. One settles in your lap like a cat. It is not glamorous, but it is going north. The wagons stop at the North Gate.

choices.label: Roll north anyway

scene_north_gate.narration: The Leaving Bell hangs over the North Gate. Beyond it lie green fields and distant Mount Red Sky. Hesper pauses for your goodbye. "No hurry," she says. "Leave however you like."

choices.label: Ring the Leaving Bell
Wave goodbye to everyone we met
Turn around and face the mountain
Look for Professor Tidewell in the crowd

check_leaving_bell.prompt: Ring the Leaving Bell loud enough for the whole city

onSuccess.narration: You haul on the rope together. BONG. The bell is so loud that every gull in the harbor lifts off at once, and all over the Exchange, people you have never met stop and wave you goodbye.

onFailure.narration: You haul on the rope, and the rope hauls back. Up you go, dangling under the bell like the world's most surprised clapper. It rings anyway. The whole gate cheers, and Hesper waits, very patiently, for you to come down.

scene_north_gate_wave.narration: You wave, and the Exchange waves back. Tobble sings a goodbye verse from the Outfitters' Steps, three keys too high. Madame Fenn's barrel rolls along the quay to keep up. "Bring me back something shiny, darlings!" High on the lighthouse, the great lamp winks twice, as if it knows something.

choices.label: Keep waving until the roofs are gone

scene_north_gate_look.narration: You turn your backs on the city and look north. Far away, over the fields, Mount Red Sky sits on the edge of the world with a little red glow on top, like a candle somebody forgot to blow out. For one blink you feel as if it is looking back. Then a wheel hits a bump, and it is just a mountain again.

choices.label: Keep your eyes on the road ahead

scene_north_gate_tidewell.narration: There she is, running alongside the wagons with an armful of soggy notes. "Count them!" shouts Professor Tidewell. "Every stone you see, count it! Write it down!" She throws you a napkin with an eight-sided shape drawn on it, trips over a goose, and keeps waving from the ground until you are out of sight.

choices.label: Fold up the napkin and keep it safe

rest_northbound.narration: That night the caravan camps in the first of the Sunward Fields, where the grass smells of honey and everybody's boots still smell of the city. Far to the north the sky glows faintly red, like a coal somebody forgot to put out. Share out your things, patch each other up, and get some sleep. The road starts properly tomorrow.

variants.text: The bags you prepared saved the fallen letters from a canal bath.

interaction_quay_line.narration: With the family's bags delivered, you join the dockhands for the last pear crates. The dockmaster fills the other gap in the line, using his hat to point when his hands are full. Not one pear drops. The last crate reaches the top of the quay, and the dockmaster tips his hat so far forward it falls off. You each get a pear for the walk to the docks, and it is the best pear in the Exchange, which is saying something this week.

choices.label: Continue together

interaction_letters.narration: Letters drift toward the canal. Wait for a clear moment, then catch them. A post clerk runs beside you with a ladle. She would prefer to keep the good news dry.

interaction.cue: Wait for the letter to float close, then grab it.

onSuccess.narration: You snatch the last letter an inch above the water. The clerk stamps it DELIVERED, even though it is not, and hurries off with her arms full of good news. You set off again, pleased with yourselves.

onFailure.narration: The last letter takes a bath in the canal. The clerk fishes it out with a ladle and decides it now smells of canal, which is a very fine smell for a letter to the harbor master. She hurries off, and you set off again.

onAssisted.narration: The clerk grabs the last letter herself, and stamps it DELIVERED, even though it is not. She hurries off with her arms full of good news, and you set off again.

interaction_jars.narration: Mrs. Tuft carries the tray beside you up the Outfitters' Steps. The pickle jar rattles at every step. She tells it sternly that the canal is not a shortcut. At the top she counts every jar and writes a tick in the air. "Good hands," she says, which from a grocer is a lot.

choices.label: Continue together

interaction_lantern_pole.narration: You stop the lantern pole while Hesper frees the washing line. The wagons wait. Long underwear floats onto a goat, which now looks like a very small caravan ghost. Hesper lifts the last peg from the hook and nods once. "On to the North Gate," she says, and the wagons roll.

choices.label: Continue together

scene_quay_wisps.narration: The dusk lamps are being lit along the quay, and the thing in your pocket is humming louder than before. Two wisps, tiny, pale and giggling, have followed the warm red stone all the way from the tavern door. They think it is a very small sun. They tangle themselves in the lamp strings, and a ferryman's rope comes loose, and his little ferry starts to drift. "Shoo them off my lamps!" he cries. "Before I am halfway to the sea!"

choices.label: Shoo the wisps off the lamps

encounter_quay_wisps.narration: The wisps zip around the lamp strings, giggling and tugging. Drive them off before the ferry drifts away.

scene_quay_wisps_shooed.narration: The wisps squeak, wobble and bob away over the water, still giggling. The ferryman hauls his rope back in, hand over hand, and ties the ferry up with a bow. "Free light," he says, and unties a bright ribbon from his best lamp string. "Take it. For luck, and for the shooing." Then he ties the lamp strings back up, and it turns out he has been hanging them in the wrong order for years.

choices.label: Head along the quay to the gem-buyers

scene_quay_wisps_scattered.narration: The wisps swirl until the whole quay is dizzy sparkles. The ferryman bangs his tin kettle against the rail, loud and honest, and the wisps pop away over the water like soap bubbles. He hauls the ferry back in and presses hot cocoa into everybody's hands. Nobody gets a ribbon tonight, but the lamps are still lit, and the cocoa is excellent.

choices.label: Head along the quay to the gem-buyers

scene_caravan_yard_thornguard.narration: The thornguard in your band plants both boots beside the lantern wagon and does not move. A pickpocket takes one look, remembers a very important appointment elsewhere, and leaves. Hesper watches all this out of the corner of one eye. "Steady," she says, which from a centaur is a medal. She hands over a long pole with a hook on the end.

choices.label: Take up your post

interaction_newcomer_load.narration: The selkie family stacks its bags on a carrying board. Raise or lower your side until it is level, then take it to the Empty Chair inn. The rocking chair rocks. The fishbowl must not.

interaction.cue: Level the carrying board before lifting the family's bags.

onSuccess.narration: You carry the bags level to the inn. The selkie children wave from their new room.

onFailure.narration: Halfway up the hill the biggest trunk pops open, and out pour about a hundred knitted socks. All five children help you chase them down the street. It takes ages, and it is the most fun anybody has had all week. The selkies take a room at the Empty Chair, socks and all.

onAssisted.narration: The selkie grandmother steadies the fishbowl while you level the board. Together you carry the bags to the inn.

interaction_post_routes.narration: Quill lays out three route cards. Share the clues and set the labeled bags in loading order. Those bags will stay by the quay for arriving letters. One envelope is addressed to THE DUCK. Quill checks that it really means the duck.

interaction.cue: Share the route cards and arrange the mail bags in loading order.
clues: The harbor bag loads before the valley bag.
The valley bag is between harbor and mountain.

onSuccess.narration: You check the sacks against the route cards. Quill gives you a brave whistle and leaves the labeled bags beside the quay for the incoming mail.

onFailure.narration: You sort the letters beautifully, into all the wrong sacks. A letter for a duke is now going to a duck. Quill sighs, says it will all come out in the wash, and stuffs everything into one enormous sack anyway.

onAssisted.narration: Quill reads the cards with you. Together you label and arrange the bags; she gives you a brave whistle for the help.

interaction_checked_mail.narration: You pocket the warm red stone. The split sack's letters flutter toward the bags you checked. Catch and pass the bundle along the quay into the right labeled bag. The clerk can keep her ladle for soup today.

interaction.cue: Catch the mail bundle and pass it to the checked bags.

onSuccess.narration: The letters reach the bags you prepared. The clerk checks the labels and carries the good news away.

onFailure.narration: A letter escapes toward the canal. The clerk catches it with her ladle and checks the bags herself.

onAssisted.narration: The clerk fills a gap beside you. Together you get the letters into the bags you prepared.

interaction_inn_account.narration: Flint makes room beside the hearth. Each hero tells a little of the red night, or adds a sound to the story. Take your time. Flint has put his nightcap over the bidding bell.

choices.label: Describe the red sky
Tell what the city did
Add a gull or harbor sound

interaction_crew_introduction.narration: Hesper lowers her clipboard. Say why your hero is going north, or name a job you can help with. Each hero gets a turn. A turnip rolls out of the cargo wagon and waits at her feet like another applicant.

interaction.cue: Each hero shares a reason to travel or a way to help.

options.label: Say why I want to go north
options.reaction: Hesper listens to your reason all the way to the end.

options.label: Offer a job I can help with
options.reaction: She writes your offered job on the crew list.

options.label: Ask Hesper what help she needs
options.reaction: Hesper explains a caravan job and leaves room for your answer.

onSuccess.narration: Hesper has heard everyone. She puts your party on the crew list.

onFailure.narration: You get muddled halfway through and say "um" eleven times. Hesper is kind about it. Hesper is also busy.

onAssisted.narration: Hesper asks one question at a time while you answer. Together you find a place for your party on the crew list.

interaction_inn_account_response_sky.narration: Your part of the sky joins the story. Flint stops counting offers. Flint thanks you for the story and gives you a warm place for the night.

choices.label: Continue together

interaction_inn_account_response_city.narration: Your memory of the city gets a nod from someone who was there. Flint thanks you for the story and gives you a warm place for the night.

choices.label: Continue together

interaction_inn_account_response_sound.narration: The room answers your sound with another. Flint laughs into his dishcloth. Flint thanks you for the story and gives you a warm place for the night.

choices.label: Continue together

voiceGuide.tone: gold-rush overture: bustling, funny, warm, a little mysterious about the red sky but never scary
forbidden: any one people owning or founding the Exchange
explaining what the gemstones really are

npcVoices.tidewell: Professor Marrow Tidewell, a selkie scholar with ink on both elbows; talks fast, draws on napkins, has been laughed out of better taverns and keeps going anyway
npcVoices.coralie_fenn: Madame Coralie Fenn, a merfolk gem-buyer in a barrel on wheels; calls everyone darlings, names enormous numbers cheerfully, never forgets a seller
npcVoices.tobble: Tobble Reedpipe, a faun cobbler who sings every price, going up a key each verse; delighted by anyone who sings back
npcVoices.hesper: Hesper Longstride, a centaur caravan master with a road-stitched sash; few words, listens to the whole answer, kind but busy
npcVoices.boggart: a rumor-selling boggart in a coat made of other coats; never says anything straight, always says it twice
npcVoices.lighthouse_keeper: a very old merfolk in a bathtub at the top of the lighthouse; firmly did not see anything
npcVoices.tour_guide: a centaur tour guide who loves the seventeen plaques and charges for every fact
npcVoices.mortar: Mortar, a stone troll noodle cook; stirs one full slow turn before answering anything, says very little, and means all of it
npcVoices.old_wick: Old Wick, a very old frogfolk lamplighter; croaks softly, wishes every lamp goodnight by name, knows the paths nobody else looks for
npcVoices.orange_captain: the yeti captain of the Sunny Disposition, an orange ship; cheerful, orange peel in his fur, pays every debt, mostly in oranges
npcVoices.postmaster_quill: Postmaster Quill, a griffin with glasses on a chain who runs the Griffin Post; squawks, loses count, insists it will all come out in the wash
npcVoices.courier_griffin: a young courier griffin, always hungry, bows with wings out to people it will remember
npcVoices.mrs_tuft: Mrs. Tuft, a sheeple grocer on a provision barge, wool full of price tags; everything comes in a jar; brisk and a little dry
npcVoices.selkie_grandmother: the grandmother of a selkie family just arrived for a fresh start; brisk, warm, decides things are settled and they are
npcVoices.innkeeper_flint: Innkeeper Flint, a stone troll who runs the Empty Chair inn in a very small nightcap; rumbles, folds his arms, secretly soft

interaction_quay_line.narration: A gap opens in the dockhands' pear-crate line. Catch and pass the crates along the quay. "Every pair of hands helps!" calls the dockmaster. His hat is sliding over his eyes.

interaction.cue: Catch the crate, then pass it down the line.

onSuccess.narration: Not one pear drops. The last crate reaches the top of the quay, and the dockmaster tips his hat so far forward it falls off. You each get a pear for the walk to the docks, and it is the best pear in the Exchange, which is saying something this week.

onFailure.narration: One crate slips, and a pear rolls all the way down the quay with a dockhand running after it. Everybody cheers when he catches it. You each get a slightly bruised pear for the walk to the docks.

onAssisted.narration: The dockmaster joins the gap in the line himself, and the crates go by smooth as a river. You each get a pear for the walk to the docks.

interaction_jars.narration: Mrs. Tuft loads a tray of jars for the Outfitters' Steps. Keep it level. One jar contains pickles; it would not mind a swim. The others would.

interaction.cue: Everyone lift or lower your side until the jars sit level, then carry the tray.

onSuccess.narration: Not a jar clinks. Mrs. Tuft counts them twice, finds every one, and writes a small tick in the air with her pencil. "Good hands," she says, which from a grocer is a lot. You carry the tray to the top of the steps.

onFailure.narration: The jars clink, tilt and slide, and one of them goes for a swim. Mrs. Tuft fishes it out with a net. "It was the pickled kind," she says. "It will not mind." You carry the rest of the tray to the top of the steps.

onAssisted.narration: Mrs. Tuft grabs one corner of the tray, and the jars settle at once. You carry it to the top of the steps together.

interaction_lantern_pole.narration: The lantern pole catches a washing line. Hold it steady while someone unhooks it. Long underwear flaps overhead. Hesper hopes it is not the new caravan flag.

interaction.cue: Friends hold the pole steady while someone unhooks the washing line.

onSuccess.narration: Click. The line comes free, and the long underwear floats down onto a very surprised goat. Not a lantern swings. Hesper nods once, and the wagons roll on to the North Gate.

onFailure.narration: The pole sways, the lanterns chime like bells, and the long underwear comes down on Hesper's head. She wears it with great dignity all the way to the North Gate.

onAssisted.narration: Hesper holds the pole steady herself and the line comes free. Not a lantern swings, and the wagons roll on to the North Gate.

interaction_inn_account.narration: Flint makes room beside the hearth. Each hero tells a little of the red night, or adds a sound to the story. Take your time. Flint has put his nightcap over the bidding bell.

interaction.cue: Each hero adds a memory or a sound from the red night.

options.label: Describe the red sky
options.reaction: Your part of the sky joins the story. Flint stops counting offers.

options.label: Tell what the city did
options.reaction: Your memory of the city gets a nod from someone who was there.

options.label: Add a gull or harbor sound
options.reaction: The room answers your sound with another. Flint laughs into his dishcloth.

onSuccess.narration: Flint thanks you for the story and gives you a warm place for the night.

onFailure.narration: Your story wanders off somewhere around the fish and never quite comes back. The prospectors laugh so kindly that Flint gives the cupboard to someone else and you the hayloft above the mules, which is warm, smells of apples, and is honestly nicer.

onAssisted.narration: Flint helps keep the story in order while you add your parts. He finds you a warm place for the night.
